records.title: Best Time to Visit East Java: Bromo, Ijen & Tumpak Sewu
records.summary: Month-by-month guide to the best time to visit Mount Bromo, Ijen blue fire, and Tumpak Sewu — the dry-season vs wet-season trade-offs for each destination.
records.answerFirst: Dry season (May-October) gives the clearest Bromo sunrises and safest Ijen night hikes; wet season (November-April) peaks Tumpak Sewu's waterfall volume. May and September are the sweet spot — dry conditions with fewer crowds than the July-August peak. JVTO runs private tours to all three destinations year-round.

records.title: Ijen Health Certificate — Real Checks, Digital Proof
records.summary: The mandatory Ijen health screening: real checks at your hotel, a BSrE-signed digital certificate, checked at the crater access gate.
records.answerFirst: Before Kawah Ijen crater entry, every guest needs a doctor-issued health certificate under BBKSDA SE.1658/K2/BIDTEK.1/KSA/9/2024. JVTO coordinates a real hotel-based screening with vitals checks and a BSrE-signed digital certificate. If a guest is not cleared, only that guest's climb is cancelled and safe-zone alternatives apply.

records.title: Packing & Fitness for Bromo, Ijen & Tumpak Sewu
records.summary: What to pack and the fitness needed for Bromo, Ijen, and Tumpak Sewu.
records.answerFirst: Fitness needs vary by destination: Mount Bromo needs only basic mobility (stepping in/out of a 4WD jeep, short walks on volcanic sand) with pre-dawn temperatures of 5-15°C at Penanjakan viewpoint — warm layers, gloves, and closed shoes are the core kit. Ijen and Tumpak Sewu demand more; see the destination sections below.

records.title: Traffic Police Escort for Tourist Groups in East Java
records.summary: How JVTO coordinates an official traffic police escort for large tourist groups in East Java — a formal request process through the Traffic Police (Ditlantas), qualifying group size, and what approval does and does not mean.
records.answerFirst: For tourist groups, usually around 18 guests or more, JVTO can request an official traffic police escort through the relevant Ditlantas unit. It is a formal approval process, not a guaranteed add-on. When approved, the escort supports road coordination on selected East Java segments.

records.title: Ijen Rijik: The Monthly Closure Day at Kawah Ijen
records.summary: Why Kawah Ijen closes on the first Friday of every month (the Rijik conservation cleanup, since March 2019) and how JVTO schedules Ijen itineraries around it.
records.answerFirst: Kawah Ijen closes to all visitors on the first Friday of every month for Rijik, a scheduled conservation cleanup running since March 2019. Park staff and volunteers typically remove an estimated 100-150 kg of waste. JVTO checks this calendar before confirming Ijen-inclusive itineraries and schedules around it.

records.title: Safety on JVTO Tours
records.summary: How JVTO plans for safety on private volcano tours and what guests should know.
records.answerFirst: JVTO's safety approach is written policy, not marketing: founder Agung Sambuko is a Tourist Police officer first, tour operator second, and every tour runs a documented Plan-B framework for volcanic closures plus a mandatory pre-hike safety briefing — guests are prepared for real conditions, not shielded from them.

records.title: Weather, Volcano Alerts & Closures
